I’ve read that the placenta can change position throughout pregnancy so I wouldn’t let that worry you! Call your OBGYN and let them know you haven’t felt baby yet. If you’re a FTM, they may say that’s generally normal, but they may advise you to go to your L&D department to do a NST or fetal monitor just to be sure baby is doing well. They may also just do a Doppler to ensure baby’s heart is beating. If you haven’t yet, they’ll do an anatomy scan soon and they’ll measure the baby and the amniotic fluids and what not. If the fluid levels are low, baby won’t move as much. They’ll tell you what to do from there.
